title: Van Ness bus lanes: the cost and the opening date, report by report
question: How far did the Van Ness bus rapid transit project move from its federal baseline?
finding: The core bus project was costed at $125.6 million in November 2012, $162.1 million when the federal agency rated it in 2014 and $189.5 million at its highest (October 2016). The whole Van Ness Improvement Project, with its sewer, water and signal work, went from $250.0 million (2014) to $346.0 million. Opening, set for 2018 in the 2014 profile, slipped to early 2019, late 2019, December 2021 and the first half of 2022; the project page says service began April 2022. The contractor claimed $6.7 million and $12 million for delays in 2019; the project started with $41.8 million in contingency and had $19.2 million left in January 2021. A June 2021 Civil Grand Jury report reviewed the delays.
how: Cost and opening date read from the Federal Transit Administration profiles of fiscal 2016 and 2017 and from ten County Transportation Authority reports and its project page; the claims and contingency figures from the July 2019 and January 2021 memos.
limits: The core cost figure fell from $189.5 million (2016) to $169.6 million (2019) without explanation in these memos, so the reports may count the core project differently over time; the whole-project figure is the steadier measure. Utility conflicts under an old street are a documented cause of delay, the claim settlement came out of budgeted contingency, and the authority only oversees: the transit agency managed construction.
